text:
Ravi Menon: Heads-up  our int8 canary shows a persistent parse-fix telemetry signal: ~0.27% parse failures are being silently repaired by the client reassembly lib, which may be masking real model regressions. we need an "repair-audit" plan.
Elena Garcia: interesting. do you have an example where repair changed meaning?
Ravi Menon: yes. raw fragments: 
```
[replica-1] ..."action": "update_profile", "args": {"name": "An
[replica-2] na", "email": null} ...
```
our conservative repair joined the quote and produced `"name": "Anna"` which looks fine, but an observed repaired case removed a trailing `null` for `email` because of a stray comma, turning `"email": null` into `"email":` and then the repair dropped the field. semantics changed.
Sofia Ruiz: that is exactly the masking risk we were worried about. repairs should be conservative and auditable. propose a repair-audit mode: repairs still attempted locally, but we store original_chunks + repaired_text + list of repair_ops to an immutable audit bucket and emit `repair_audit:1` telemetry. then an offline comparator runs semantic-diff checks against a golden set and flags possible masking.
Aisha Kapoor: agree. implementation sketch: 
- repair-audit flag (runtime config) toggles storing: {call_id, model, quant, canary_id, original_chunks_blob, repaired_text, repair_ops, timestamp, caller_hash}
- small HMAC/cid to avoid sensitive payload retention; default scrub PII fields via existing redaction pipeline.
- run nightly comparator: for each audited item, compute args equality (exact) and semantic similarity of `repaired_text` vs `non-repaired` fallback (if we requested non-streaming full-response) using embedding cosine. if args differ or similarity < 0.85, mark as potential masking.
Elena Garcia: how do we get the non-repaired ground truth? we could trigger a non-streaming fetch for a sampled subset (counts against retry budget) and store that alongside the repair audit.
Ravi Menon: exactly. repair-audit runbook: attempt repair -> if repair succeeds and repair-audit on, queue an async non-streaming fetch (sampled 1/50 repairs) -> store both versions for comparator. if non-streaming fetch fails or times out, mark as `no_ground_truth`.
Sofia Ruiz: telemetry additions: `repair_attempted`, `repair_ops` (enum list), `repair_outcome` (fixed|abstained|ruled_out), `repair_audit_logged` (0/1), `repair_mask_candidate` (0/1). tag with model, quant_mode, canary-id.
Aisha Kapoor: we also need policy: if repair_mask_candidate rate > 0.1% over 24h for a canary, auto-disable repairs for that canary and fall back to strict parsing + non-streaming retry. create an alert for on-call.
Ravi Menon: storage and privacy notes: redact PII before storing; store only a short-lived window (30 days) for audit. keep the comparator job in infra/secure.
Elena Garcia: for the comparator, besides embedding similarity, add a small function-call arg comparator: compare parsed JSON objects field-by-field using tolerant rules (null vs missing = warn, changed scalar value = fail). compute a single `mask_score` per item.
Sofia Ruiz: nice. also add a canary experiment: enable repair-audit for 5% traffic for one week on staging and prod-mirror. gather mask_score distribution and false-positive rate by hand review.
replay-bot: repair-audit canary deployed to eng-ml staging (5311112250) at 5% traffic  audit queue enabled.
Aisha Kapoor: I'll wire up an alert dashboard: daily mask_rate, repair_ops histogram, masked_items_for_review. ops will auto-disable repairs for canary if daily mask_rate > 0.1% per policy.
Ravi Menon: thanks. follow-ups: Elena will own comparator heuristics, Sofia will add telemetry + policy, Aisha will add the alerting and runbook, I'll instrument the sample non-streaming fetch logic. please post first 24h report back in this thread. :thumbsup:
